rejectedSkills.reason:
NOT a quality rejection — this is a strong, in some respects stronger, candidate than the incumbent. Blocked purely by an id collision: research/manifests/design-review.json already holds a decided 'vendor' manifest for the exact same id (plugin87/ux-ui-agent-skills, rubric 3/3/1/1=8), and the catalog/index.json entry for 'design-review' already reflects that same content (confirmed by reading catalog/index.json directly), i.e. it is already shipped. Writing a second manifest at the same path would silently overwrite decided work rather than flag a collision, so this is recorded here for curator attention instead.

Why it is worth a second look: this humbleteam version is fully self-contained (one internal relative link to references/review-rubric.md, zero externally-bundled files) versus the incumbent's four bundled files pulled in from outside its own directory (workflows/design-review.md, accessibility/wcag-checklist.md, scripts/contrast.py, taste/design-taste.md) via a portability modification — so it would score conformance 2 against the incumbent's 1. It also has a distinct, more elaborate mechanism the incumbent lacks: explicit mode detection across four modes (review / comparison / advisory / grounded-advisory) with a first-match-wins routing rule and a worked example for each, a five-band 0-4 score with an explicit tie-break rule ('the cost of the fix decides the band, not the violation count'), and a capped 3-6 issues-by-impact rule with a mandatory Before/After/Why format citing a numbered Nielsen heuristic, a WCAG 2.2 success criterion, or a named platform guideline. If vendored on its own merits it would score relevance 3, quality 3, conformance 2, uniqueness 1 (real overlap with the incumbent's Nielsen-heuristic-citation mechanism, but the four-mode routing and tie-break rule are not present there) = 9, higher than the incumbent's 8.

Recommendation for the curator: consider swapping this humbleteam version in for the currently-shipped design-review, or merging the tie-break/mode-routing ideas into the incumbent, rather than treating this inspection as a pass.
